decisions.reason: Confirmed nonfatal dimension-notation defect: the old k-coordinate p could not multiply an m-coordinate X when k differs from m. The acceptance clause now explicitly takes probability row p and row X on [m], with scalar sum_i p_i X_i; divergence also explicitly uses a common finite set. Entropy, divergence, stochasticity and all numerical claims are preserved.

Confirmed nonfatal row/column notation defect: a row times the transpose of a matrix column is undefined. Define X_j as the transpose of column j, preserving every acceptance formula and quantitative bound. Direct expansion gives sum_j q_j D^(j) A X_j^T=sum_x D_x C_xx>=0.99 and sum_j q_j DA X_j^T=D C D^T<=||D||_2^2+0.01<=0.02; zero-weight posteriors equal D and contribute zero. No probabilistic or quantitative claim is weakened.

Confirmed nonfatal omitted-hypothesis restatement: F4 incorrectly omitted nonnegativity, although every application is to density operators (or to their nonnegative diagonal tensor products). F4 now states the full relevant equivalence, and F7 likewise explicitly assumes a nonnegative endomorphism. In eigenbases Delta has real eigenvalues lambda_i and tau has t_j>=0 summing to one; the product trace norm is sum_ij |lambda_i|t_j=sum_i |lambda_i|. Both tensor products are positive trace-one states, and the factor 1/2 is preserved. The Statement and proof remain unchanged.

False positive: the Definition gives a finite randomized procedure and labels what its output declares; it asserts no bounded-error guarantee for arbitrary E and r. The separate thm-qa-35-fingerprint-correctness-and-cost explicitly assumes positive relative distance delta and chooses r=ceil(ln(1/epsilon)/(-ln(1-p0))), with p0=delta-delta^2/2. For distance 1 at length N, one-test false equality probability is (1+(1-1/N)^2)/2; its possible proximity to one is consistent with the procedure and theorem. The code-state supplier admits all code maps, normalizes N=1 as well, and the fresh controls, wirewise Fredkin gates and finite stopping rule are well-defined.
